item.title: Maximal Curves with Few Automorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.37777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of constructing maximal curves with few automorphisms over finite fields. Our main ingredient is the determination of the \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\!\left(\overline{\mathbb F}_p\right)\)-stabilizer of the roots of the Chebyshev polynomials, apart from two exceptional cases already treated in the literature. We prove that, in all other cases, the only nontrivial M\"obius symmetry is the sign involution. This settles the general case for the automorphism groups of the corresponding Chebyshev curves. We further construct an infinite family of maximal curves of unbounded genus whose only nontrivial automorphism is the hyperelliptic involution. This reveals a contrasting phenomenon to the common heuristic that curves with many rational points tend to have large automorphism groups.
item.dc:creator: Herivelto Borges, Lucas Reis

item.title: Spectrahedral relaxations and tightenings of rigidly convex sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.37850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a natural spectrahedral relaxation of a rigidly convex set (rcs) that depends only on the cubic part and on the degree of the defining real zero polynomial. For quadratic polynomials, we prove exactness and for a product of linear polynomials, we show that a higher order version of our relaxation is exact. We also establish a way of tightening the relaxation by moving the origin inside the rcs, and that the rcs is recovered by sweeping the origin over its interior. To obtain all these results we use a linear form that is closely connected to the zeros of a given real zero polynomial. We also prove that any rcs can be written as an affine linear slice of the cone of non-negative polynomials. Using this, we can define a hierarchy of tightenings that are spectrahedral shadows. We can show that this tightening is exact if the given polynomial admits a determinantal representation. This tightening is similar to a tightening of a hyperbolicity cone due to Kummer, Plaumann, and Vinzant.
item.dc:creator: David Sawall, Markus Schweighofer

item.title: Calabi-Yau Hyperbolicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.37996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this paper is to introduce a new notion of hyperbolicity for compact complex manifolds with trivial canonical bundle, called \textit{Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity}. We investigate its fundamental properties and establish a characterization in terms of the fundamental group. In particular, we show that no compact K\"ahler Calabi--Yau manifold is Calabi--Yau hyperbolic, highlighting the genuinely non-K\"ahler nature of this notion. We also investigate different techniques for constructing examples of such manifolds. Finally, we examine the relationship between Calabi--Yau hyperbolicity and Kobayashi hyperbolicity in the examples considered, highlighting obstructions to the latter in the Calabi--Yau setting.
item.dc:creator: Abdelouahab Khelifati

item.title: Pointed Hurwitz--Brill--Noether theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.38023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the geometry of Hurwitz--Brill--Noether spaces with vanishing conditions at a totally ramified point. Degeneration to a curve with an elliptic tail simplifies the combinatorics of Larson, Larson--Larson--Vogt, and Aggarwal, giving inductive proofs of Aggarwal's results in the one-point setting, and yields an efficient recursion for the algebraic Euler characteristics. Finally, when the expected dimension is negative, we give a numerical criterion ensuring the universal Hurwitz--Brill--Noether locus admits a component of expected relative dimension, generically finite over its image in the Hurwitz space, analogous to the existing results of Pflueger and Teixidor i Bigas for classical Brill--Noether loci.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Bud, Richard Haburcak

item.title: A curve of genus $2$ over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and hexads of bitangents to a smooth quartic
item.description: arXiv:2610.38071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the Abel-Jacobi map of a genus 2 curve over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ arising from a double cover of $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ branched along six lines. We utilize the so-called Mumford representations to conduct the calculations. As an application, we give an alternative proof of classical results on quartics and bitangents. Furthermore, we obtain a method to give explicit defining equations of quartic curves that have the six lines as bitangents and apply it to determine the number of connected components of the realization space.
item.dc:creator: Shinzo Bannai, Hiro-o Tokunaga

item.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
item.description: arXiv:2610.38137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting K\"ahler-Ricci solitons. It recovers the usual Miyaoka-Yau inequality in the K\"ahler-Einstein case. Our proof uses weighted equivariant Bogomolov-Gieseker and Langer inequalities for torsion-free sheaves, together with a weighted slope estimate for the canonical extension sheaf. We also construct toric examples showing that the existence of a soliton implies neither weighted semistability of the canonical extension sheaf nor nonnegativity of the equivariant Miyaoka-Yau number.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Hisamoto, Masataka Iwai

item.title: Asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ of stable pointed curves and the all-light Hassett spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0|n}$, for fixed genus $g\ge1$ as the number of markings tends to infinity. We prove central limit theorems for the full Betti distributions, whose variances grow linearly in $n$ with leading coefficients independent of the genus. For the normalized even Betti numbers, we establish refined local limit theorems with estimates uniform in degree. These local estimates yield asymptotic formulas for individual even Betti numbers and determine the sharp central ultra-log-concavity thresholds $\frac{3(e-2)}{2(3-e)}$ and $3$, respectively. For $g\ge2$, the off-diagonal Hodge components form proportions of exact orders $n^{-1/2}$ and $n^{-1}$ of the total cohomology of the two spaces, respectively. The conditional distributions of the Hodge difference $p-q$ given $p\ne q$ converge, for both spaces, to a single discrete law independent of the genus. We also prove that tautological classes account for all but a proportion of exact order $n^{-1}$ of the even cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$. The tautological degree distribution converges to the standard Gaussian under the centering and scaling of the ambient even Betti distribution. An explicit asymptotic formula for the ratio of the ordinary Euler characteristics of the light and heavy spaces answers a question of Kannan, Serpente and Yun. The proofs combine the heavy/light substitution with a stratification of the light spaces by stable cores, singularity analysis of Hodge generating functions, and refined Fourier estimates exploiting Poincar\'e duality.
item.dc:creator: Jinwon Choi, Young-Hoon Kiem

item.title: Geometry of $m$-direct-sum morphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.38184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V$ be a complex vector space of dimension $mk$ ($m\ge2$). A morphism from a positive-dimensional projective variety $f\colon X\to\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$ is $m$-direct-sum if $V=U_{x_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus U_{x_m}$ for every $m$ pairwise distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_m$ on $X$, where $U_x\subset V$ is the subspace represented by $f(x)$. We show that $X$ is necessarily a smooth rational curve. When the so-called drill $d(f)$ of $f$ is $1$ or when the rank $k$ is at most $2$, we give complete classifications of $f$ up to the automorphisms of $\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$. As applications, we classify all so-called skew scrolls in $\mathbb{P}^3$, which completely answers a question of Day. Then we show that if $X\subset \mathbb{P}(V)$ is a smooth, projective, nondegenerate subvariety whose higher-order Terracini locus is empty, then $X$ is the rational normal curve, which strengthens the critical Terracini rigidity discovered by Ballico and Chiantini. By using the same machinery, we also prove a dual version of Terracini rigidity. Finally, we show that $m$-unisolvent systems form an abelian category of finite length and that $7$ is the least diagonal exponent of a simple rank-three $2$-unisolvent system.
item.dc:creator: Duo Li, Yanjie Li, Francesco Russo

item.title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.38187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla's special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of \cite[Remark 2.4]{BLMM17}, pointed out by Bruinier--Zuffetti \cite{BZ26}. Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily--Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Li, Zelin Ye

item.title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds of type K
item.description: arXiv:2610.38298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Calabi-Yau threefold of type K is a free quotient $X=(S\times E)/G$ of the product of a K3 surface and an elliptic curve. We construct a family of geometric Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$ by using Liu's product construction on $S\times E$ and then inducing along the Galois covering. The family has dimension $2h^{1,1}(X)$, and is disjoint from the $\widetilde{\GL}_2^+(\R)$-orbit of Li's stability conditions. These threefolds carry a K3 fibration, and the pushforward of an object from a smooth K3 fiber is (semi)stable if and only if it is (semi)stable on the K3 surface.
item.dc:creator: Uttaran Dutta

item.title: On the Witt liftability of quasi-F-split Calabi--Yau varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.38427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a quasi-$F$-split strict Calabi--Yau variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of odd characteristic $p$ admits a smooth projective lifting over $W(k)$ if $p\geq d-1$, or if $p=d-2$ and $H^0(X,T_X)=0$. We also prove $W_3(k)$-liftability in odd characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Teppei Takamatsu

item.title: Sheaves on quoric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.38456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quoric manifolds are quaternionic analogues of quasitoric manifolds introduced by Hopkinson. Given a quoric manifold over a simple polytope, we study the stratification induced by the faces of the polytope. We then show that the equivariant derived category of constructible sheaves with respect to the face stratification is equivalent to the derived category of constructible DG-modules over a DG-algebra defined on the orbit space. Finally, we prove that the associated DG-algebra is formal.
item.dc:creator: Christos Aravanis, Ioannis Gkeneralis

item.title: On the motivic approach to the Abhyankar rectifiability problem and concrete rectifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.38474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study closed embeddings of the complex affine line into affine three-space. We prove that, for every such embedding, the complete-intersection normal map identifies the $\mathbb{A}^1$-fundamental sheaf of its complement with $\mathbf{K}_2^{\mathrm{MW}}$. The proof compares torsors under arbitrary strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves. A nodal projection expresses a torsor by a normal parameter and finitely many node parameters. Extension across the node axes gives equations for the latter. Their correction terms increase a nilpotent filtration generated by the Milnor-Witt symbols of the branch-height differences. We deduce the vanishing of the first Alexander sheaf of every complex embedded line. We also construct polynomial rectifications using finite inverses and affine modifications, including rectifications of the Shastri trefoil and a harmonic figure-eight over $\mathbb{Z}[a]/(a^2-a+1)$, with arbitrary base change. The companion repository (https://github.com/qft98romanov-hash/abhyankar-moh-trefoil) contains explicit rectifiers, their inverses, proofs, and symbolic checks. We prove that a normal map with a polynomial section and geometric generic affine-line fiber is a coordinate projection. We formulate the remaining rectifiability and descent questions; the general complex rectifiability problem is not settled here. An appendix treats other fields, normal orientations, and arithmetic descent.
item.dc:creator: A. S. Frolov, I. S. Dorofeev

item.title: On the Supersingular reduction of Cubic fourfolds with Complex Multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2610.38498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: If $X$ is a K3 surface with complex multiplication by a CM field $E$, Kazuhiro Ito proved that the height of the reduction of $X$ in characteristic $p>0$, and its Artin invariant if it is supersingular, can be computed from the decomposition of $p$ in $E$. We present analogous results for cubic fourfolds by using the main theorem of complex multiplication for cubic fourfold, proved by Rikuto Ito.
item.dc:creator: Temma Yamagishi

item.title: Equivalence of freeness and higher order freeness of hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2610.38550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using vector bundle theory, we prove that an essential hyperplane arrangement in an $\ell$-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero is free if and only if its module of logarithmic derivations of order $p$ is free for some $1\le p\le\ell-1$. The same statement holds for multiarrangements.
item.dc:creator: Takuro Abe

item.title: Existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for weighted complete intersections
item.description: arXiv:2610.38727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every smooth well formed Fano or Calabi-Yau weighted complete intersection admits a nef-partition. As an application, we establish the existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for all such Fano weighted complete intersections.
item.dc:creator: Victor Przyjalkowski, Constantin Shramov

item.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.38736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang's descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, K\"ahler--Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan

item.title: Examples of rigid Twistor D-modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.38751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The well-established theory of D-modules gives a framework to study linear differential equations from the perspective of algebraic geometry. A significant advancement in this theory has been the introduction of Twistor D-modules by Claude Sabbah and Takuro Mochizuki: These objects expose inherent, but hidden information of the underlying differential equations in an elegant way. We explain the foundational concepts of Twistor D-modules and give concrete examples of these objects. We introduce a notion of rigidity for Twistor D-modules, which these examples fulfill. We conclude with a certain algebraicity conjecture about rigid Twistor D-modules, which we prove in a special case.
item.dc:creator: Patrik Hammer

item.title: Dimensions of Fano schemes of lines on hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.38812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbb{C}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$. We prove that an $m$-dimensional integral projective family of lines sweeping a variety of dimension $y$ satisfies $m\le\max\{2y-d-1,n-3\}$. This proves the de Jong-Debarre conjecture for $d\le n$ and the Beheshti-Starr bound for lines on smooth hypersurfaces for $d\ge n+1$.
item.dc:creator: Chenglong Yu

item.title: Intrinsic Non-Reductive Geometric Invariant Theory and Moduli Spaces of Principal Bundles with Non-Reductive Structure Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.38837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of moduli spaces for algebraic stacks with a weak action of $\Theta = [\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m]$ (including stacks of filtered objects and unstable $\Theta$-strata) for which the center admits a good moduli space and the retraction to the center has flat, finitely presented relative inertia, providing a stack-intrinsic generalization of the existence of non-reductive Geometric Invariant Theory quotients. As an application, we construct quasi-projective coarse moduli spaces of principal bundles over a smooth projective curve with non-reductive structure groups, including moduli spaces of Ramanathan unstable principal bundles of fixed Harder--Narasimhan type.
item.dc:creator: George Cooper, Ludvig Modin

item.title: A Gasch\"utz Lemma for linear algebraic groups with applications to the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2610.38919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Gasch\"utz Lemma states that for a surjective morphism $G\to H$ of finite groups, generators $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ of $H$ can be lifted to generators $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ of $G$, provided that $G$ can be generated by $d$ elements. We prove an analog of this statement for linear algebraic groups. This has applications to the algebraic-geometric theory of linear differential equations: We show that every regular singular differential embedding problem over the rational function field has a regular singular solution. We also establish a purely algebraic variant of the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence on the punctured projective line that works over any countable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
item.dc:creator: Jason Bell, Michael Wibmer

item.title: Amitsur groups of Imprimitive Fano Threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.38963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify possible Amitsur groups of smooth imprimitive Fano threefolds defined over $\cc$ that admit a faithful action of a finite group.
item.dc:creator: Shreya Sharma

item.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.38972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and give examples of smooth connected spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Nikolaev

item.title: Logarithmic transformations on the six-sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.39102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there are infinitely many choices of the multiplicities in the logarithmic transformation step of the Alp\"oge--Claude construction which produce a complex threefold diffeomorphic to the six-sphere. Moreover, distinct choices of the multiplicities yield biholomorphically inequivalent complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Viaclovsky

item.title: The inverse local-relative correspondence and the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation for the local Gromov--Witten theory of smooth weak del Pezzo surfaces, by identifying its unique formal solution with the inverse of the local-relative correspondence. We construct this inverse through an associative set-partition convolution and establish the identification using Zagier's recursion for the Bloch--Okounkov $n$-point function. The proof applies in all genera and includes non-toric surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jianjun Fu, Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang

item.title: Generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and unirationality of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.39284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and study their relation to quasi-\'etale double covers. As an application, we prove that a del Pezzo surface of degree $2$ over an infinite field of characteristic different from $2$ is unirational if it has a rational generalized Eckardt point. This resolves a previously open case not covered by Manin's construction.
item.dc:creator: Runxuan Gao

item.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
item.description: arXiv:2610.39336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X=V_5$ be the quintic del Pezzo threefold. Along the negative zero-tilt-slope paths for rational-curve ideal classes, degree five is the first degree admitting a positive point correction. We determine the resulting degree-five outer good moduli space: it is reduced with exactly two irreducible components, a normal ten-dimensional principal branch and a smooth corrected branch $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Their scheme-theoretic intersection is a normal determinantal ninefold. Along its singular locus, the principal branch has transverse rank-one $2\times 4$ determinantal singularities, while the intersection has the corresponding $2\times 3$ singularities. We construct an explicit small resolution of the principal branch as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petkovi\'c--Rota Kuznetsov-component sixfold along its point locus. Uniform wall exclusion and point-correction bounds for degrees two through five establish the first correction threshold; the corrected degree-five factors are precisely the ideals of elliptic linear sections parametrized by $\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$.
item.dc:creator: Zheyuan Fu

item.title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two. Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle. More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic N\'eron--Severi lattice. The key new result is the congruence property of the subgroup generated by reflective involutions in $O(U\oplus N)$ for anisotropic even lattices $N$ of signature $(1,1)$. Combined with the local generation theorem and Chow-theoretic criterion of Li--Yu--Zhang, this gives the required reflective decompositions and their consequences for zero-cycles.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyuan Li

item.title: Balancing tautological intersection numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.39462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the three balancing inequalities conjectured by the authors about 20 years ago: moving one unit from a larger index to a smaller one cannot decrease a mixed tautological intersection number, whether the two distinguished insertions are psi classes, kappa classes, or Hodge Chern classes.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

item.title: Poincar\'e series of degree-two Chow varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.39498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C_{p, 2}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the Chow variety parametrizing effective algebraic $p$-cycles of degree two on $\mathbb{P}^{n}$. We show that its rational cohomology is pure Tate and concentrated in even degrees. An anti-invariant Chern class identity yields a presentation of the cohomology ring as a fiber product, which in turn determines the cohomology over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$. We identify the ordinary Poincar\'e polynomial with the known virtual formula, determine the optimal ranges over which the coefficients stabilize, and compute the nonrational Poincar\'e series of the stable space $D(2)$. For the Lawson--Michelsohn map $D(2)\longrightarrow D(\infty)$, the first nonzero rational homotopy kernel occurs in degree eight and is one-dimensional, while the integral kernel has rank one. Finally, we compute the relative homology of the pair $(D(2),BU)$ over $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$ and show that additional cohomology generators and nonzero rational homotopy kernels arise in unbounded degrees.
item.dc:creator: Youming Chen, Wenchuan Hu, Deyuan Ma

item.title: Automorphism groups of smooth quartic threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.39627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify finite groups of automorphisms of smooth quartic threefolds over $\mathbb{C}$. Every such group embeds into one of $17$ maximal groups, which we realize by explicit equations and matrix generators. Among finite subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}(5,\mathbb{C})$ preserving a smooth quartic threefold, there are exactly $24$ maximal ones up to conjugacy, and we use them to determine the $194$ groups that occur as full automorphism groups. As an application, we classify the finite groups of projective automorphisms of smooth quartic surfaces and show that there are exactly $12$ maximal ones up to conjugacy in $\mathrm{PGL}(4,\mathbb{C})$.
item.dc:creator: Zigang Zhu

item.title: Solid Arithmetic D-modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.39799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a solid ring of arithmetic differential operators analogue to Berthelot's D-dagger, and its derived infinity-category of solid quasi-coherent modules. We show that there is a fully faithful functor from Berthelot's derived category of bounded complexes of D-dagger-modules with coherent cohomology into our new category.
item.dc:creator: Kolar David (IRMAR)

item.title: The Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in dimensions three and four
item.description: arXiv:2610.39838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, confirming the Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.
item.dc:creator: Dongjian Wu, Nantao Zhang

item.title: Compatibility of Perverse Truncation of Ng\^o Fibrations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study compatibility of perverse truncations for morphisms between Ng\^o fibrations with rationally smooth total spaces. We show that, under an effective rank inequality, equivariant pullbacks preserve the normalized perverse truncations. Applied to the diagonal, this gives multiplicativity of perverse truncations for Hitchin systems with rationally smooth total spaces.
item.dc:creator: Bin Wang, Shihao Wang, Chenglong Yu

item.title: A Yau-Tian-Donaldson correspondence for degenerations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an equivalence between the existence of a unique K\"ahler-Einstein metric on a degeneration of Fano varieties and uniform CM minimization. This proves a discretely valued analogue of the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture, in the sense of non-Archimedean geometry. As a main tool, we prove that Ding stability of a degeneration implies uniform Ding minimization, proving a converse to work of Blum-Xu. We also prove an analogous result in geometric invariant theory (GIT), stating that uniform GIT height minimization of a family of points is equivalent to GIT stability, proving a converse to work of Wang, Wang-Xu and the author.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Frey

item.title: On Terao's conjecture for at most nine planes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note we show that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of at most nine planes in the complex projective $3$-space. Moreover, we show that every essential and irreducible free arrangement of at most nine planes in $\mathbb{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is divisionally free, and we list all intersection lattices of such arrangements. Our approach is based on Ziegler's restriction theorem and a simple count involving the numbers of multiple lines. As a by-product, we show that Cynk--Szemberg octic arrangements are never free. Finally, motivated by a recent work of Dimca and Pokora, we present examples of weak Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements, including pairs of octic arrangements leading to rigid double octic Calabi--Yau threefolds.
item.dc:creator: Bartosz Jaros{\l}awski

item.title: Degenerate complex structures on surfaces and stability conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical heuristics suggest that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions of a projective Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ should be related to the moduli space of complex structures on its mirror $X^\vee$. On the other hand, recent work in the literature introduces a modular partial compactification, $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$, of a quotient of the space of stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}^{b}(X)$. We provide some mathematical evidence for the aforementioned heuristics by proving that for curves and surfaces, certain boundary strata in $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ describe degenerate complex structures on $X^\vee$. Along the way, we introduce a criterion for producing boundary points of $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ when $\mathcal{D}$ is an arbitrary $k$-linear triangulated category. As a byproduct, we deduce the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on certain quotients of the derived categories of K3 and Enriques surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Antonios-Alexandros Robotis, Nicol\'as Vilches

item.title: Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.40074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface. Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve. Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is constant in linear series on K3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Richard Haburcak

item.title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.40097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected K\"ahler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.
item.dc:creator: Simon Pietig

item.title: The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two. We also prove numerical dimension zero and construct the unique projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal minimal model. Its Picard number is one and its canonical divisor has order two. The perfect cone compactification is a Mori dream space, and the birational automorphism group of $\mathcal{A}_6$ is trivial. The proof combines normal vanishing on the Prym locus, polar intersections on abelian boundary fibers, and an exact theta calculation. A discrepancy estimate recovers the modular open subset from the minimal model.
item.dc:creator: Haowu Wang

item.title: The $6\frac{1}{2}$-functor formalism of Cartier modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.40200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime. We construct a coherent formalism of geometric operations on Cartier modules with coefficients in ind-coherent sheaves on noetherian derived $\mathbb F_p$-schemes. For such a scheme $X$, we consider the stable presentable category $\mathrm{Cart}(X)$ of ind-coherent sheaves $M$ equipped with a structural morphism $F_{*,X}M \to M$, where $F_X$ denotes the Frobenius endomorphism. We construct pushforward functors for arbitrary morphisms and exceptional pullback functors for separated morphisms almost of finite type, together with coherent composition and base-change equivalences. We single out conditions under which these functors admit further adjoints. On derived schemes separated and almost of finite type over $\mathbb F_p$, we construct compatible closed symmetric monoidal structures given by shriek tensor products, and establish which functors are symmetric monoidal. The constructions arise from a general procedure for forming functor formalisms of Cartier objects, using their description as lax limits and the universal properties of span $2$-categories developed by Cnossen--Lenz--Linskens [arXiv:2505.19192].
item.dc:creator: Klaus Mattis, Timo Wei{\ss}

item.title: Galois module structure of Deligne--Lusztig varieties for $\mathrm{GL}_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)\to\overline{\mathbf{X}}(w)$ be the ramified Galois cover of compactified Deligne--Lusztig varieties. Our objects of study are the Lefschetz numbers for the action of the finite covering group $T^{wF}$ on the coherent cohomology of the structure sheaf of $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$. The Lefschetz numbers for all elements of $T^{wF}$ determine the virtual $T^{wF}$-representation given by the alternating sum of these cohomology groups. In the two cases of Deligne--Lusztig surfaces of type $A_2$ and ${}^{2}A_2$, we give explicit formulas for the Lefschetz numbers for a generator of the stabilizer of an irreducible component. It follows that the equivariant Euler characteristic of the compactification $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$ is not virtually free as a virtual module over the covering group.
item.dc:creator: Adithya Sathyanarayana

item.title: Degeneration of (-1)-shifted symplectic stacks and categorification of Donaldson-Thomas invariants
item.description: arXiv:2610.40336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study cohomological Donaldson-Thomas invariants of perfect complexes in a semistable degeneration of projective Calabi-Yau threefolds, with smooth components $X_1,X_2$ meeting along a smooth anticanonical surface $S$. The generic fiber of degeneration family is a $(-1)$-shifted symplectic stack. Over the special fiber, the derived restriction to $S$ is derived Lagrangian, and its homotopy fiber product is also $(-1)$-shifted symplectic. Our goal is to relate the categorical DT invariants of the generic fiber moduli, induced by periodic cyclic homology of matrix factorization category of 0-shifted potential functions over such moduli, to that of the special fiber obtained via derived Lagrangian intersection and geometric quantization. This is achieved via construction of a flat Gauss-Manin connection that relates the generic fiber cohomological DT invariants to that of the special fiber. The geometric framework, universal trace diagrams, and fourfold foliation were developed jointly with Jacob Kryczka in arXiv:2510.20325. Here we construct ordinary critical realizations, oriented cyclic-to-bar comparisons, and Gauss-Manin operators, and verify finite specialization in explicit moduli problems. We workout our construction via several explicit examples such as Grassmannians, Relative Hilbert Schemes and moduli space of pure 2 dimensional sheaves with support moving in a fixed linear system of divisors in the ambient threefold.
item.dc:creator: Artan Sheshmani

item.title: Moduli space of irregular singular $\lambda$-connections and the relative symplectic form
item.description: arXiv:2610.40352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the moduli space of $\lambda$-connections with ramified singularities on a smooth projective curve $X$. We construct a quasi-projective relative moduli scheme $M^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Hod}} \to \Lambda$ of $\alpha$-stable $\lambda$-connections over a base parameter space $\Lambda$. This moduli space connects the irregular de Rham moduli space ($\lambda=1$) and the irregular Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs bundles equipped with non-zero irregular local exponents ($\lambda=0$). Furthermore, we show that $M^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Hod}}$ is smooth over $\Lambda$ and carries a canonical relative symplectic form $\omega_{M^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Hod}}/\Lambda}$, yielding a natural Poisson structure on the total space.
item.dc:creator: Michi-aki Inaba, Arata Komyo

item.title: Asymptotic GIT-stability of KSB-stable varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.40583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that KSB-stable varieties introduced by Koll\'ar and Shepherd-Barron as a generalization of Deligne-Mumford's stable curves are stable in the sense of geometric invariant theory (GIT). More precisely, we show that KSB-stable varieties are asymptotically GIT-stable with respect to a sequence of linearizations defined by the Hodge bundle.
item.dc:creator: S\'andor J Kov\'acs, Behrouz Taji

item.title: Partial Airy ideals and coloured blobbed topological recursion
item.description: arXiv:2610.33232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define and study the notion of partial Airy ideals, which are certain linear systems of PDEs that may contain less equations than variables. We show that they admit a unique solution of exponential type (the partition function) modulo a choice of initial condition. We construct a large class of examples of partial Airy ideals attached to spectral curves using twisted free-field representations of $\mathcal{W}(\mathfrak{gl}_r)$-algebras at self-dual level. This generalizes the results of Bouchard- Borot-Chidambaram-Creutzig-Noshchenko by significantly enlarging the set of admissible spectral curves, provided they come with additional data that we call colour. We show that the differential constraints on the partition function are equivalent to a set of equations on the associated correlators, which we call coloured loop equations. We find a recursive residue formulation for the solutions of those equations, the coloured blobbed topological recursion}, which is a generalization of the currently known forms of topological recursion. It includes the blobbed topological recursion of Borot-Shadrin as a special case, giving it a natural interpretation within the formalism of partial Airy ideals.
item.dc:creator: Ga\"etan Borot, Vincent Bouchard, Swagata S. Datta

item.title: Moment Polyptychs and the Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.37724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric variety of complex dimension $2n$ using symplectic cutting. When the defining arrangement is cooriented so that its base region is non-empty and bounded, fibre rotation has proper moment map and produces compact K\"ahler orbifold cuts carrying the residual torus action. We introduce the moment polyptych of such a cut, a polytopal complex assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and show that its vertices and local lattice data determine the fixed points, tangent weights, and finite orbifold groups required for equivariant orbifold Riemann-Roch localisation. Even for a smooth hypertoric manifold, a reducible core forces every cut in the outer cut chamber to have non-trivial cyclic isotropy, while the cuts are smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety, which is then a product of projective spaces. For a positive regular integral level $d$ in the outer cut chamber, algebraic cutting identifies the cut's quantisation with a finite filtration piece of the circle-graded quantisation of the original hypertoric variety, whose successive quotients recover the individual circle-weight spaces. We prove that the higher cohomology of the pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes at every such level, so that the localised index is the character of the actual space of sections. Finally, a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is the arrangement slack function, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. Thus, each finite stage admits a weighted lattice-point description whose multiplicity function is supported on the lattice points in the support of the level-$d$ moment polyptych.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin C. W. Brown

item.title: Geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack
item.description: arXiv:2610.38115v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The analytic Emerton-Gee stack is a rigid analytic moduli stack of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules over the Robba ring, and is expected to play a fundamental role in the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for locally analytic representations. In this paper, we establish the fundamental geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack: it is a rigid analytic Artin stack, normal, a local complete intersection, and equidimensional of the expected dimension. As an application, our normality result removes the reducedness hypothesis in the paper of Le, Strauch, and Wang, thereby yielding an unconditional proof of the conjecture on the global sections of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack formulated by Emerton, Gee, and Hellmann.
item.dc:creator: Yutaro Mikami

item.title: Test ideals can be computed by boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.38163v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $R$ be a normal $F$-finite ring of characteristic $p>0$. We show that one effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $\Delta$, with $K_R+\Delta$ $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$, computes the big test ideal. This answers a question of Schwede and Smith. More generally, we prove their conjecture that test module of a Cartier algebra acting on an ideal is the test module of a single map $\psi$ in the algebra and even the image of $\psi$. We prove a global version for schemes quasi-projective over an $F$-finite local ring as well. In particular, every such normal, locally strongly $F$-regular scheme admits an effective boundary $\Delta$ for which $(X,\Delta)$ is locally strongly $F$-regular and $K_X+\Delta$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Ajit, with Appendix joint with Daniel Apsley

item.title: An analogue of $\Gamma$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
item.description: arXiv:2610.38371v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $\Gamma$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Finkelberg, David Kazhdan

item.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
item.description: arXiv:2610.38376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.
item.dc:creator: Hairun Wang

item.title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.38414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity. The main analytic difficulty is to obtain estimates uniform over lattices of unbounded determinant. We address this by combining a reduction based on primitive sublattices of codimension one and least determinant with explicit bounds for theta norms and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.
item.dc:creator: Haowu Wang, Shaoyun Yi

item.title: Nevanlinna Theory on Berkovich Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.38435v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a value distribution theory for finite analytic morphisms between proper connected quasi-smooth Berkovich curves over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. The central tool is a multi-tail Dirichlet Green function on finite truncations of a generalized skeleton, which makes non-Archimedean potential theory on skeleta compatible with global Nevanlinna asymptotics. Using it, we prove the first main theorem as an exact identity relating the characteristic, counting, and proximity functions. For logarithmic targets we establish a second main theorem in both ramified and level-one truncated forms. The defect relation is also given. The theory provides a Berkovich-analytic framework for non-Archimedean value distribution, bridging classical Nevanlinna theory and its $p$-adic counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Tingbin Cao, Jiahu Peng

item.title: Projected Brion's theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an analogue of Brion's theorem for the projected integer-point transform. Brion's theorem writes the integer-point transform of a rational polyhedron $P$ as the sum of the rational functions associated to its vertex cones. The pushforward $\pi_*$ along a lattice projection $\pi$ turns the transform of $P$ into the generating function of the numbers of lattice points in the fibres of $\pi$. We group the vertices of $P$ into contracted classes, generated by the edges whose direction $\pi$ kills, and show that the sum of the rational functions associated to the vertex cones in a contracted class can be pushed forward along $\pi$, yielding a rational function decomposition of the projected integer-point transform. For a lattice polytope, the classes correspond to the connected components of the fixed locus of the associated toric variety under the action of a subtorus, and our formula resembles the localization formula for this subtorus. We use this decomposition to provide an explicit formula for the projected integer-point transform of a linear family of polytopes. We illustrate this result with families of Gelfand--Zetlin and string polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Dupraz, Leonid Monin

item.title: Comparing metric completions of triangulated categories with Verdier quotients
item.description: arXiv:2610.39035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neeman's metric on a triangulated category assigns lengths to morphisms and allows us to construct triangulated metric completions of the category. We prove that the metric completion of a triangulated category with respect to a constant metric is always a subcategory of the Verdier quotient by the thick subcategory generated by cones of zero-length morphisms, and we provide a sufficient criterion for equality. To that end, we define continuous functors between completions which induce triangulated functors between completions. Moreover, we give two applications. First, we show that the additive equivalence discovered by Cummings and Gratz between the Paquette-Yildirim completion and a specific metric completion of an Igusa-Todorov discrete cluster category is, in fact, a triangulated equivalence. Second, we fully classify metric completions of bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves over weighted projective lines of domestic or tubular type.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Matou\v{s}ek

item.title: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.39364v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes from genus-two curves over finite fields. Let $C_\mathcal{ L}(D,G)$ be such a code over $\mathbb F_q$, with length $n$ and dimension $k$. Assume that $3\leq k\leq n-3$. We prove that $n<(2q+10\sqrt q+16)/3$. This bound holds for every prime power $q$ and for both parities of $k$. It gives a uniform upper bound of $2q/3+O(\sqrt q)$ for the maximal length. The explicit bound is strictly smaller than $q+1$ when $q\geq125$.
item.dc:creator: Haojie Chen

item.title: On equivariant affineness in elliptic cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2610.39583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate equivariant affineness in spectral algebraic geometry: the phenomenon where $\infty$-categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of a spectral stack are equivalent to $\infty$-categories of modules over an equivariant ring spectrum. In the nonequivariant case, this is known as 0-affineness, and has been studied by Gaitsgory, Mathew--Meier, amongst others. Allowing for equivariant phenomena opens up a much wider class of spectral stacks to be studied through the lens of spectra. The spectral stacks at the heart of our analysis are oriented elliptic curves, their associated Hilbert schemes, and related constructions. When working over the universal base, so the moduli stack of oriented elliptic curves, we show that these spectral stacks are $U(1)$-, $U(n)$-, and $SU(n)$-equivariantly affine, with associated $G$-ring spectrum Gepner--Meier's equivariant topological modular forms $\mathrm{TMF}_G$. Our results also encompass the groups $Sp(n)$ as well as all finite products of such groups. Our most general result is a relative statement over an arbitrary base stack. These results can be viewed as an integral and global refinement of Greenlees' algebraic model for modules over rational $U(1)$-equivariant elliptic cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Jack Morgan Davies, Sil Linskens, Leonard Tokic

item.title: Formality transmission
item.description: arXiv:2610.39767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Across mathematics, formality results are usually established through general criteria rather than by constructing explicit equivalences. These criteria include domination, puncturing, highly-connected formality, intrinsic formality, formality descent, formality in families, purity, etc. In this article, we prove that all these criteria are instances of a single theorem, formality transmission. This unifying framework allows us to extend these criteria in several directions, beyond characteristic zero and to differential graded algebras over operads or properads, leading to diverse new formality results.
item.dc:creator: Coline Emprin

item.title: A dynamical approach to Frobenius splitting
item.description: arXiv:2610.40392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A dynamical system can be associated to the process of decomposing iterated Frobenius pushforwards of modules into indecomposable direct summands. Via this connection, we apply the theory of Markov chains to study asymptotic counts of multiplicities of indecomposable summands in the iterated Frobenius pushforwards of the given module, as the number of iterations grows. Our results recover and extend the existing results on the existence of the (generalized) F-signature due to Hashimoto--Symonds, Hashimoto--Kobayashi, Smith--Van den Bergh, Tucker, and Yao. We also develop further the theory of F-contributors, the modules for which the multiplicity grows at the maximal possible rate. As a key algebraic input, we define and develop strongly F-regular modules, extending Hochster--Huneke's notion of strongly F-regular rings. We use strongly F-regular modules to prove convergence of the relevant sequences and algebraically characterize F-contributors, when the underlying ring admits a module-finite strongly F-regular extension or has dimension at most two.
item.dc:creator: Alapan Mukhopadhyay, Ilya Smirnov

item.title: Finite-rank rigidity and Nash-curve discreteness for correlation potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.40475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every nonconstant real polynomial P of degree k and every positive rational exponent a/b, minimizing the spherical energy with potential |P(t)|^{a/b} admits a discrete solution with at most $\binom{d+2ak-1}{2ak}+\binom{d+2ak-2}{2ak-1}$ support points, where a/b is reduced. This finite-replacement consequence needs no denominator threshold. Under a multiplicity-sensitive denominator condition, we prove the stronger conclusion that every minimizer has an explicit uniform support bound; suitable negative positive-semidefinite perturbations preserve that bound. We present these consequences before the machinery. The main arguments simplify irrational-power finite-rank rigidity and give a Nash-curve ramification obstruction, stable under entire scalar additions, for powers, logarithms, and rational poles. The latter yields uniform finite supports on compact semialgebraic curves without assuming that the supports are semialgebraic. The known p-frame finite-replacement principle is distinguished from the extensions developed here. No unconditional discreteness theorem for general irrational p is claimed.
item.dc:creator: Josiah Park

item.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, reduced and immersed
item.description: arXiv:2610.40602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a `reduced' form of permutation twisted cohomology as introduced by Balmer--Gallauer and further developed by Miller. This ring is bigraded by a well-chosen choice of endotrivial complex, rather than multigraded by a family of endotrivial complexes. The Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules openly immerses into the homogeneous spectrum of this ring. We also show that for $p$-groups, Miller's `remixed' twisted cohomology ring also admits the Balmer spectrum as an open subspace, and confirm in both cases it can be upgraded to have Dirac scheme structure; furthermore, we prove that the two open covers witnessing this are in general different.
item.dc:creator: Juan Omar G\'omez, Sam K. Miller

item.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.40622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate counting problems for discrete (geometric) structures in tropical settings, motivated by the comparison of the expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games. First, we give an upper bound on the number of coherent matching fields of type $(n,r)$ and a lower bound on the number of combinatorial types of $n$-hyperplane sequences in the max-plus tropical space of dimension $r-1$. These structures are closely related, and our bounds establish that as $n \to \infty$, for every fixed $r$ their number equals $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$. This in turn implies that the number of regular triangulations of the products of simplices $\Delta^{n-1}\times\Delta^{r-1}$ is also $n^{(r-1)^2n+o(n)}$, thereby answering a question of Santos. Second, we obtain that the number of labeled order types over the reals and over the signed tropical numbers coincide at first order, establishing a comparison of the expressivity of mean-payoff games and linear programs as measured by labeled order types. Last, the subclass of mean-payoff games known as parity games arise from linear programs by a ``double tropicalization.'' We show that the number of labeled order types obtained after this double tropicalization collapses.
item.dc:creator: Xavier Allamigeon, Yiyuan Chen, St\'ephane Gaubert, Xavier Goaoc

item.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.40639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that all compact hyperk\"ahler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojevi\'c and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact K\"ahler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Pio Contr\`o

item.title: Enumeration of plane unicuspidal curves of any genus via tropical geometry
item.description: arXiv:1807.11443v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We enumerate complex curves on toric surfaces of any given degree and genus, having a single cusp and nodes as their singularities, and matching appropriately many point constraints. The solution is obtained via tropical enumerative geometry. The same technique applies to enumeration of real plane cuspidal curves: We show that, for any fixed $r\ge1$ and $d\ge2r+3$, there exists a generic real $2r$-dimensional linear family of plane curves of degree $d$ in which the number of real $r$-cuspidal curves is asymptotically comparable with the total number of complex $r$-cuspidal curves in the family, as $d\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Yaniv Ganor, Eugenii Shustin

item.title: Volumes of moduli spaces of flat surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2004.03198v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the moduli spaces of flat surfaces with prescribed conical singularities. Veech showed that these spaces are diffeomorphic to the moduli spaces of marked Riemann surfaces, and endowed with a natural volume form depending on the orders of the singularities. We show that the volumes of these spaces are finite. Moreover we show that they are explicitely computable by induction on the Euler characteristics of the punctured surface for almost all orders of the singularities.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Sauvaget

item.title: Topology of irregular isomonodromy times on a fixed pointed curve
item.description: arXiv:2208.02575v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We will define and study (moduli) spaces of deformations of irregular classes on Riemann surfaces, which provide an intrinsic viewpoint on the `times' of irregular isomonodromy systems in general. Our aim is to study the deeper generalisation of the G-braid groups that occur as fundamental groups of such deformation spaces, with particular focus on the generalisation of the full G-braid groups.
item.dc:creator: Jean Dou\c{c}ot, Gabriele Rembado

item.title: Wall divisors on irreducible symplectic orbifolds of Nikulin-type
item.description: arXiv:2209.03667v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the wall divisors on irreducible symplectic orbifolds which are deformation equivalent to a special type of examples, called Nikulin orbifolds. The Nikulin orbifolds are obtained as partial resolutions in codimension 2 of a quotient by a symplectic involution of a Hilbert scheme of 2 points on a K3 surface. This builds on the previous article arXiv:2009.04873 in which the theory of wall divisors was generalized to orbifold singularities.
item.dc:creator: Gr\'egoire Menet, Ulrike Riess

item.title: On the decomposition group of a nonsingular plane cubic by a log Calabi-Yau geometrical perspective
item.description: arXiv:2402.13968v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper aims to study the decomposition group of a nonsingular plane cubic under the light of the log Calabi-Yau geometry. Using this approach we prove that an appropriate algorithm of the Sarkisov program in dimension 2 applied to an element of this group is automatically volume preserving. From this, we deduce some properties of the (volume preserving) Sarkisov factorization of its elements. We also confirm an expectation by Blanc, Pan and Vust on the splitting property of the canonical complex of a nonsingular plane cubic. Within a similar context in dimension 3, we exhibit in detail an interesting counterexample for a possible generalization of a theorem by Pan in which there exists a Sarkisov factorization obtained algorithmically that is not volume preserving.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Alves da Silva

item.title: Fourier-Mukai partners of abelian varieties and K3 surfaces in positive and mixed characteristics
item.description: arXiv:2410.14065v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Fourier-Mukai equivalences of (families of) abelian varieties and K3 surfaces in positive and mixed characteristics. We first prove in any characteristics that Fourier-Mukai partners of abelian varieties are again abelian varieties. We subsequently focus on the canonical lifts of ordinary abelian varieties and ordinary K3 surfaces. For such schemes, we show that Fourier-Mukai equivalences on the special fibers can be lifted to the canonical lifts. We also prove that the relative Fourier-Mukai partners of the canonical lifts are in bijection with the Fourier-Mukai partners of the special fibers. We conclude by demonstrating that the last result can be used to recover the ordinary case of a result originally proved by Honigs, Lombardi and Tirabassi.
item.dc:creator: Riku Kurama

item.title: Criteria for a fiberwise Fujiki/Kahler family to be locally Moishezon/projective
item.description: arXiv:2503.07548v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we utilize the theory of non-K\"ahler loci by S. Boucksom to construct an integral $2$-cohomology class whose restriction to a general fiber is big, and then construct a relatively big line bundle via the exponential sequence. This leads to a local Moishezonness criterion for fibrations whose total spaces are compact complex manifolds in the Fujiki class $\mathscr{C}$, generalizing the bimeromorphic version of F. Campana's local projectivity theorem. We further combine a similar idea with the singular Demailly--P\u{a}un theorem by T. Collins--V. Tosatti to obtain a local projectivity criterion for fibrations from compact K\"ahler manifolds, yielding a new proof and a generalization of F. Campana's local projectivity theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen

item.title: Prekosmic Grothendieck/Galois Categories
item.description: arXiv:2504.20949v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a generalized version of the duality between groups and the categories of their representations on sets. Given an abstract symmetric monoidal category $K$ called Galois prekosmos, we define pre-Galois objects in $K$ and study the categories of their representations internal to $K$. The motivating example of $K$ is the cartesian monoidal category $\textit{Set}$ of sets, and pre-Galois objects in $\textit{Set}$ are groups. We present an axiomatic definition of pre-Galois $K$-categories, which is a complete abstract characterization of the categories of representations of pre-Galois objects in $K$. The category of covering spaces over a well-connected topological space is a prototype of a pre-Galois $\textit{Set}$-category. We establish a perfect correspondence between pre-Galois objects in $K$ and pre-Galois $K$-categories pointed with pre-fiber functors. We also establish a generalized version of the duality between flat affine group schemes and the categories of their linear representations. Given an abstract symmetric monoidal category $K$ called Grothendieck prekosmos, we define what are pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$ and study the categories of their representations internal to $K$. The motivating example of $K$ is the symmetric monoidal category $\textit{Vec}_k$ of vector spaces over a field $k$, and pre-Grothendieck objects in $\textit{Vec}_k$ are affine group $k$-schemes. We present an axiomatic definition of pre-Grothendieck $K$-categories, which is a complete abstract characterization of the categories of representations of pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$. The indization of a neutral Tannakian category over a field $k$ is a prototype of a pre-Grothendieck $\textit{Vec}_k$-category. We establish a perfect correspondence between pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$ and pre-Grothendieck $K$-categories pointed with pre-fiber functors.
item.dc:creator: Jaehyeok Lee

item.title: Rank three representations of Painlev\'e systems: I. Wild character varieties
item.description: arXiv:2505.21186v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give explicit cubic equations for the wild character varieties corresponding to the rank 3 representations of Painlev\'e equations, and compare them to the ones of their classical rank 2 representations.
item.dc:creator: Miklos Eper, Szilard Szabo

item.title: The classification of quasi-elliptic fibrations and unexpected plane cubics in characteristics 2 and 3
item.description: arXiv:2510.06365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we categorize all isomorphism classes of quasi-elliptic surfaces over a field $k$ of characteristic 2 or 3. For every quasi-elliptic surface $X$, we classify all possible sequences of blow-downs from $X$ to the projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2_k$. We then use these categorizations to identify all unexpected plane cubic curves in characteristic 2 and present a proof of the lack of unexpected cubics in characteristic 3. Before the work in this paper -- based partly on the author's thesis -- the complete classification of unexpected plane cubic curves in characteristic 2 was unknown, as well as the question of the existence of unexpected plane cubic curves in characteristic 3.
item.dc:creator: Jake Kettinger

item.title: Borel subalgebras of Lie algebras of vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2510.17223v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In [I. Arzhantsev and M. Zaidenberg, Borel subgroups of the automorphism groups of affine toric surfaces, arXiv:2507.09679 (2025)] we described the Borel subgroups and maximal solvable subgroups of the automorphism groups of affine toric surfaces. In the present paper, we introduce the notion of an integrable Borel subalgebra in the Lie algebra of the automorphism group of an affine variety. We show that they are precisely the tangent algebras of the Borel subgroups. We classify the integrable Borel subalgebras in the Lie algebras of the automorphism groups of toric affine surfaces, notably of the affine plane and its cyclic quotients.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Arzhantsev, Mikhail Zaidenberg

item.title: Relative $\mathbb{A}^1$-Contractibility of Koras-Russell Prototypes and Exotic Motivic Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2510.21594v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Koras-Russell threefolds are a certain family of smooth, affine contractible threefolds exhibiting "exotic" behavior in the algebro-geometric context. Our goal in this note is to extend its $\mathbb{A}^1$-contractibility from a field to a general base scheme. As a consequence, we also give a general strategy to extend the $\mathbb{A}^1$-contractibility of Koras-Russell prototypes in higher dimensions over a general base scheme. As a major consequence, we establish the existence of "exotic" motivic spheres in all dimensions at least 4 over infinite perfect fields.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Kumar Madhavan Vijayalakshmi

item.title: The Cone Conjecture for Enriques Surfaces in any Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2604.05827v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a proof of the Morrison-Kawamata cone conjecture for Enriques surfaces independent of their characteristic. It is based on the analysis of certain generically finite morphisms of degree two.
item.dc:creator: Simon Brandhorst, Gebhard Martin, Tobias Schnieders

item.title: Surfaces with canonical map of odd degree
item.description: arXiv:2604.09216v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S$ be a smooth complex minimal surface of general type with $p_g:=h^0(K_S)\ge 4$ whose canonical map is generically finite of odd degree $d>1$ onto a surface $\Sigma$. We assume that the general canonical curve of $S$ is smooth and that $\Sigma$ is ruled by lines, and we prove: - $p_g\le d+2$ - $\Sigma$ is a cone over the rational normal curve of degree $p_g-2$ in ${\mathbb P}^{p_g-1}$ - $p_g=d+2$ can occur only for $d=3,9,11$. As a byproduct, we refine previous results by Beauville and Xiao by proving that if one drops the assumption that $\Sigma$ is ruled by lines then $d\le 5$ if $p_g\ge 112$. The case $d=3$ being completely classified by the first two named authors, we focus on $d=5$, showing that $p_g\le 5$ and that for $p_g=5$ the surface $S$ has a pencil $|C|$ with $C^2=1$ and $K_SC=5$. These results suggest that the answer to the question whether the surfaces with canonical map of odd degree $d>1$ have bounded invariants could be positive, in sharp contrast with the case of even degree.
item.dc:creator: Margarida Mendes Lopes, Rita Pardini, Roberto Pignatelli

item.title: Normal Functions, Even Theta Characteristics and the Theta Divisor
item.description: arXiv:2604.21661v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $[C]$ be a point in the moduli space of curves $\mathcal{M}_g$, with $g>1$, lying outside a countable union of closed nowhere--dense subsets of an analytic parameter space for $\mathcal M_g$. Let $G \,\subset\, J(C)$ be a connected compact subgroup of real dimension $1$ of the Jacobian of $C$, and let $L$ be an even theta characteristic on $C$. We prove that $\{\zeta \, \in\, G\ \big\vert\,\ H^0(C,\, L \otimes \zeta)\,\not=\, 0 \}\, =\, \emptyset$ if and only if $L \otimes \zeta_G$ is an even theta characteristic on $C$, where $\zeta_G$ is the unique non-trivial point of $G$ of order two.
item.dc:creator: Indranil Biswas, Lorenzo Fassina, Gian Pietro Pirola

item.title: The $\mathbf{P}^1$-motivic Gysin map
item.description: arXiv:2604.24888v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a $\mathbf{P}^1$-unstable non-$\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant theory of motivic spaces and spectra, and construct the Gysin map therein for regular immersions. This in particular gives the Gysin map in the Annala--Hoyois--Iwasa $\mathbf{P}^1$-motivic spectra, and thus gives a uniform construction for the Gysin maps of various cohomology theories.
item.dc:creator: Longke Tang

item.title: Anti-Zariski pairs
item.description: arXiv:2606.20268v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1929, O. Zariski found a pair of complex plane algebraic curves of the same degree and with the same collection of singularities, but embedded into the plane in a topologically different way. Accordingly, such curves belong to different components of the equisingular family. This phenomenon has been intensively studied till now. In this note, we propose a different insight on this subject: Two curves $C',C''\subset\PP^2$ form an {\it anti-Zariski pair}, if $(\PP^2,C')$ and $(\PP^2,C'')$ are homeomorhic, but $C'$ and $C''$ belong to different components of the equisingular family. We exhibit examples of anti-Zariski pairs and discuss related issues.
item.dc:creator: Peng Ren, Eugenii Shustin

item.title: Obstructions to embedding singular curves in toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2607.18475v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every integer $d \geq 2$, we show that there exists an irreducible, reduced curve which embeds in $\mathbb{P}^d$ but in no projective normal toric variety of dimension less than $d$. In particular, there exist reduced irreducible curves that embed in $\mathbb{P}^d$ but do not embed in any weighted projective space of dimension less than $d$.
item.dc:creator: Maya Banks, Izzet Coskun, Kevin Tucker

item.title: Notes on the Kuznetsov component of cubic sevenfolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.28784v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $Y$ be a cubic 7-fold. When $Y$ is smooth, its Kuznetsov component is a Calabi-Yau category of dimension 3, and we construct an embedding of the Kuznetsov component into the derived category of Clifford modules over $\mathbb{P}^4$. When $Y$ is a general cubic 7-fold singular along a line, we construct an explicit weakly crepant categorical resolution of its Kuznetsov component by the derived category of a smooth Calabi-Yau 3-fold, recovering a result of Favero-Kelly. In this construction, we express the resolution functor explicitly as a composition of geometric functors and mutations, and identify its kernel with a category equivalent to a pull-back of the derived category of a stacky curve.
item.dc:creator: Peize Liu

item.title: Essential $p$-dimension and Chern numbers
item.description: arXiv:2608.08877v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth, projective, connected variety over a field $k$ containing a root of unity of order $p$. If $X$ has a Chern number prime to $p$, we show that every finite $p$-group acting on $X$ acts through a subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_n(k)$, where $n=\dim X$. This allows one to transfer properties of representations of finite $p$-groups to their actions on $X$. We deduce a fixed-point theorem which, unlike earlier results of this kind, is sensitive to the arithmetic of the base field, and whose dimensional bound is sharp for each individual group (apart from one low-dimensional case when $p=2$). We also obtain restrictions on finite $p$-groups of birational automorphisms of rationally connected varieties; for instance the Cremona group $\operatorname{Cr}_n(\mathbb{Q})$ contains no element of order $p^2$ when $p \ge n+2$. More generally, we prove variants of these results in the presence of a Chern number not divisible by a given power of $p$. The method is based on the following observation about the essential $p$-dimension $\operatorname{ed}_p(G)$ of an affine algebraic group $G$: over a field of characteristic zero, the number $\operatorname{ed}_p(G) + \dim G$ is the least dimension of a smooth projective variety $Y$ with a generically free $G$-action such that the degree map $\operatorname{CH}_G(Y) \to \mathbb{F}_p$ from the equivariant Chow group is nonzero. The Chern numbers modulo $p$ of $Y$ lie in the image of this map; combined with Karpenko and Merkurjev's computation of the essential $p$-dimension of finite $p$-groups, this yields our results.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Haution

item.title: The Multivariable Strong Monodromy Conjecture for Plane Curves
item.description: arXiv:2608.26087v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the multivariable Strong Monodromy Conjecture for the local topological zeta function of arbitrary tuples of nonzero nonunit plane curve germs. The entries may be nonreduced and may have common irreducible factors. We also prove that the non-equivariant local motivic and topological zeta functions have the same polar locus and generic pole orders, using a multivariable extension of the Nicaise--Xu definition of motivic pole order. Our arguments combine twisted Poincar\'e residues with resolution formulas and specialization to one variable. In arbitrary dimension, we prove that a nonzero iterated residue class on a stratum of a log resolution implies the vanishing of the Bernstein--Sato ideal at the corresponding parameter. In particular, every topological polar hyperplane whose order equals the ambient dimension is contained in this zero locus. For algebraic germs, the topological pole order is at most the motivic pole order, and the two attain maximal order simultaneously.
item.dc:creator: Sheng Tan

item.title: The derived length of subgroups of the Cremona group
item.description: arXiv:2609.08876v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the maximal derived length of a solvable subgroup of the plane Cremona group over $\mathbb C$ is equal to $5$. The main difficulty is the case of subgroups containing loxodromic elements. To treat this case, we prove that the maximal derived length of a finite solvable subgroup is $4$ and establish a centraliser theorem: the centraliser of a finite solvable subgroup of derived length $4$ contains no loxodromic element. The proof of the centraliser theorem relies on Blanc's classification of maximal algebraic subgroups and then uses equivariant Sarkisov theory, orbit estimates, superrigidity, and fixed curves of genus at least two.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Philippe Furter, Isac Hed\'en

item.title: The geometry of solutions to the general sextic
item.description: arXiv:2609.30422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the geometry of the three simplest known formulas for roots of a general sextic polynomial. In contrast with work of Green on the quintic, we show that no "simultaneous uniformization" of the normal forms associated to the solutions exists. This demonstrates an intrinsic qualitative complexity of sextic equations that is not present in quintic equations.
