Additionally, we give a formula for the roots of a general sextic in terms of Hilbert modular cusp forms and the uniformizing differential equation of the associated Hilbert modular surface.
item.dc:creator: Sidhanth Raman

item.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26186v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001, for Batyrev's mirror pairs of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces and its orbifold generalization, without assuming that the lattice points in the defining reflexive polytope generate the ambient lattice. We then identify the pushforward of the extended hypersurface \(I\)-function with a generating series of normalized compact periods of the mirror, providing a period interpretation of the hypergeometric series governing ambient genus-zero orbifold Gromov--Witten theory. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.
item.dc:creator: Tsung-Ju Lee

item.title: There are no unexpected toric positroid varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.35914v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a positroid. We prove that the positroid variety $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to some algebraic torus if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is regular. In that case, $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to the standard diagonal torus. Thus, there are no unexpected toric positroid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Avery McNeill

item.title: Local wild mapping class groups and cabled braids
item.description: arXiv:2204.08188v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We will define and study some generalisations of pure $\mathfrak{g}$-braid groups that occur in the theory of connections on curves, for any complex reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. They make up local pieces of the wild mapping class groups, which are fundamental groups of (universal) deformations of wild Riemann surfaces, underlying the braiding of Stokes data and generalising the usual mapping class groups. We will establish a general product decomposition for the local wild mapping class groups, and in many cases define a fission tree controlling this decomposition. Further in type A we will show one obtains cabled versions of braid groups, related to braid operads.
item.dc:creator: Jean Dou\c{c}ot, Gabriele Rembado, Matteo Tamiozzo

item.title: Gromov-Witten Generating Series of Elliptic Curves and Iterated Integrals of Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
item.description: arXiv:2310.08018v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute various types of iterated integrals of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms that are constructed from the Kronecker theta function. Furthermore, we relate the generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves to these iterated integrals.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Communications in Number Theory and Physics, Vol. 20, Issue 2 (2026), pp. 309-351
item.dc:creator: Jie Zhou

item.title: Diamonds: Homology and the Central Series of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2310.08283v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an analog of a theorem of Stallings which asserts the homomorphisms between the universal nilpotent quotients induced by a homomorphism $G \to H$ of groups are isomorphisms provided a pair of homological conditions are satisfied. Our analogy does not have a homomorphism between $G$ and $H$ but instead $G,H \leq G_0$ that satisfies a similar homological condition. We derive a few applications of this result. First, we show that there exist pairs of non-isomorphic number fields whose absolute Galois groups have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. We show that there exists pairs of non-isometric hyperbolic $n$-manifolds whose fundamental groups are residually nilpotent and have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. These are the first examples of residually nilpotent Kleinian groups with arbitrarily large nilpotent genus. Complex hyperbolic 2-manifold examples are given as well. Considering Riemann surfaces and complex hyperbolic 2-manifolds as projective curves and surfaces defined over a number field, we show the (outer) action of the absolute Galois group of the field of definition on the universal nilpotent quotients of the geometric fundamental groups are equivalent. This is in contrast to fact that the (outer) Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve determines the curve by work of Mochizuki. In particular, the nilpotent representation theory of the geometric fundamental group is not anabelian.
item.dc:creator: Milana Golich, D. B. McReynolds

item.title: The Einstein-Hilbert functional and the Donaldson-Futaki invariant
item.description: arXiv:2310.11625v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a Kaehler manifold polarised by a holomorphic ample line bundle, we consider the circle bundle associated to the polarisation with the induced transversal holomorphic structure. The space of contact structures compatible with this transversal structure is naturally identified with a bundle, of infinite rank, over the space of Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein-Hilbert functional of the associated Tanaka-Webster connections is a functional on this bundle, whose critical points are constant scalar curvature Sasaki structures. In particular, when the group of automorphisms is discrete, these critical points correspond to constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics in the first Chern class of the polarisation. We show that the Einstein--Hilbert functional satisfies some monotonicity properties along some one-parameter families of CR-contact structures that are naturally associated to test configurations, and that its limit on the central fibre of a test configuration is related to the Donaldson-Futaki invariant through an expansion in terms of an extra real parameter. As a by-product, we obtain an original proof that the existence of constant scalar curvature Kaehler metrics on a polarized manifold implies K-semistability. We also show that the limit of the Einstein-Hilbert functional on the central fibre coincides with the ratio of the equivariant index characters pole coefficients of the central fibre.
item.dc:creator: Abdellah Lahdili, Eveline Legendre, Carlo Scarpa

item.title: Monoidal structures on triangulated fibered categories
item.description: arXiv:2401.13491v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a small category admitting binary products. There exists a canonical dictionary expressing the structure and properties of monoidal $\mathcal{S}$-fibered categories in terms of the external tensor product in place of the usual internal tensor product. In this paper, we specialize this dictionary to the setting of triangulated $\mathcal{S}$-fibered categories, by studying how the general translation process interacts with shift functors. Our results provide a satisfactory abstract framework to study monoidal structures from the perspective of perverse sheaves.
item.dc:creator: Luca Terenzi

item.title: Approximation of adelic divisors and equidistribution of small points
item.description: arXiv:2407.14978v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the Galois orbits of generic sequences of algebraic points of small height in a projective variety over a number field. Our main result is a generalization of Yuan's equidistribution theorem that applies to heights for which Zhang's lower bound for the essential minimum is not necessarily an equality. It extends to all projective varieties a theorem of Burgos Gil, Philippon, Rivera-Letelier and the second author for toric varieties. It also applies to sums of canonical heights for an algebraic dynamical system, and in particular it recovers K\"uhne's semiabelian equidistribution theorem. We also generalize previous work of Chambert-Loir and Thuillier to obtain new logarithmic equidistribution results. Finally we extend our main result to the quasi-projective setting recently introduced by Yuan and Zhang.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Balla\"y, Mart\'in Sombra

item.title: Amplituhedra and origami, I: tree level
item.description: arXiv:2410.09574v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a precise correspondence between points of the $m=4$ tree momentum amplituhedron and origami crease patterns. As an application, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ tree amplituhedron both in momentum space and in momentum-twistor space. As another application, we show that every nondegenerate weighted planar bipartite graph $\Gamma$ admits a t-embedding, i.e., an embedding of the planar dual of $\Gamma$ such that the sum of angles of white (equivalently, black) faces around each vertex is equal to $\pi$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Galashin

item.title: An Unexpected Rational Blowdown
item.description: arXiv:2510.00115v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rational blowdown operation in 4-manifold topology replaces a neighborhood of a configuration of spheres by a rational homology ball. Such configurations typically arise from resolutions of surface singularities that admit rational homology disk smoothings. Conjecturally, all such singularities must be weighted homogeneous and belong to certain specific families: Stipsicz-Szab\'o--Wahl constructed QHD smoothings for these families and used Donaldson's theorem to obtain very restrictive necessary conditions on the resolution graphs for singularities with this property. In particular, these results, as well as subsequent work of Bhupal-Stipsicz, show that for certain resolution graphs, the canonical contact structure on the link of the singularity cannot admit a QHD symplectic filling. By contrast, we exhibit Stein rational homology disk fillings for the contact links of an infinite family of rational singularities that are not weighted homogeneous, producing a new symplectic rational blowdown. Inspiration for our construction comes from de Jong-van Straten's description of Milnor fibers of sandwiched singularities; we use the symplectic analog of de Jong-van Straten theory developed by the second and third authors. The unexpected Stein fillings are built using spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations.
item.dc:creator: M\'arton Beke, Olga Plamenevskaya, Laura Starkston

item.title: Quivers with involutions and shifted twisted Yangians via Coulomb branches
item.description: arXiv:2510.12118v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To a quiver with involution, we study the Coulomb branch of the 3d $\mathcal{N} = 4$ involution-fixed part of the quiver gauge theory. We show that there is an algebra homomorphism from the corresponding shifted twisted Yangian to the quantized Coulomb branch algebra. This gives a new instance of 3D mirror symmetries.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Communications in Mathematical Physics 407 (2026), Paper No. 244
item.dc:creator: Yaolong Shen, Changjian Su, Rui Xiong

item.title: K\"ahler-Einstein toric submanifolds of the projective space
item.description: arXiv:2512.03617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the K\"ahler-Einstein metrics on the four families of symmetric toric Fano manifolds due to Batyrev and Selivanova cannot be induced by immersions into projective spaces equipped with the Fubini-Study metric. We also show a similar conclusion for the non-symmetric examples discovered by Nill and Paffenholz. As an application we obtain that a centrally symmetric toric Fano manifold admits a K\"ahler-Einstein metric induced by a projective immersion if and only if it is a product of projective lines. These results confirm for each of these examples a broader conjecture characterizing the K\"ahler--Einstein metrics that can be induced by projective immersions.
item.dc:creator: Antonio J. Di Scala, Mart\'in Sombra

item.title: The Poincar\'e polynomial of the type B analogue of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n+1}$
item.description: arXiv:2603.01956v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomial of the type B analogue of the Deligne--Knudsen--Mumford moduli space of rational curves with n marked points, providing type B counterparts to results by Keel, Manin, Getzler, and Yuzvinsky. We establish functional and differential equations satisfied by the bivariate exponential generating function of these polynomials. We show how this generating function relates to the classical one in type A. We deduce the gamma-positivity of these polynomials via a quadratic recursion and discuss a type B analogue of a formula found by Aluffi, Marcolli and Nascimento in type A.
item.dc:creator: Luis Ferroni, Roberto Pagaria, Lorenzo Vecchi

item.title: Perverse filtration on the cohomology of affine Springer fibers
item.description: arXiv:2606.01507v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the top cohomology of any affine Springer fiber, as a Weyl group representation, contains a large part of the total cohomology of certain Springer fibers. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of a ``perverse filtration'' on the pure part of the cohomology of affine Springer fibers.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwei Yun

item.title: Amplituhedra and origami, II: loop level
item.description: arXiv:2606.03439v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Building on the recently discovered origami-amplituhedron correspondence, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ amplituhedron in full generality at all loop orders, both in momentum and momentum-twistor space. Along the way, we develop two natural "$L$-punctured" extensions of the positive Grassmannian and relate them via T-duality.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Galashin

item.title: Rank-Two Drinfeld Modules over Elliptic Coordinate Rings
item.description: arXiv:2606.26851v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let ${\mathbf A}$ be the affine coordinate ring of $E\setminus\{\infty\}$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $\infty$ is rational. We solve the rank-two case of the open problem of explicitly classifying sign-normalized Drinfeld ${\mathbf A}$-modules in generic characteristic with a fixed determinant motive; the classification for rank greater than two remains open. Outside an explicit exceptional locus, the rank-two Drinfeld modules are parametrized by the open modular curve $Y^{q+1}=\pi(X)$ with $Y\neq0$. The polynomial $\pi$ is squarefree, and the smooth projective completion of this curve has genus $q^2$. The roots of $\pi$ split into two types. Above roots of the first type, all coefficient functions extend regularly, and their extensions yield exactly the exceptional modules. Roots of the second type correspond to cusps of the modular curve; above these roots, the coefficient family has poles.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Ze-Dong Huang, Chang-An Zhao

item.title: Abelian Orbifolds for Brane Brick Models
item.description: arXiv:2606.28110v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a systematic procedure for constructing brane brick models corresponding to abelian orbifolds of toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds, extending the orbifold construction beyond the well-studied case of abelian orbifolds of C^4. Given a parent brane brick model corresponding to a toric Calabi-Yau 4-fold M, we show that the action of an abelian orbifold group Gamma on the generators of M induces an action on the chiral and Fermi fields as well as the J- and E-terms of the associated 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theory. The requirement that the orbifolded brane brick model remains consistent with the closed paths associated with the J- and E-terms, together with the chiral cycles formed by their products, precisely reproduces the Calabi-Yau condition on the orbifold action. This procedure yields an explicit formula for the J- and E-terms of the orbifolded brane brick model in terms of those of the parent theory. We apply our construction to the brane brick models corresponding to Q^{1,1,1} and D_3, and present the resulting families of 2d (0,2) quiver gauge theories. We also present explicit expressions for generating functions that count distinct abelian orbifolds of Q^{1,1,1} and D_3.
item.dc:creator: Juno Kwon, Rak-Kyeong Seong

item.title: Bad Reduction of Genus Two Curves with complex multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2609.22544v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study genus two curves whose Jacobians have complex multiplication by a biquadratic CM field. In this setting the Jacobian decomposes as a product of two elliptic curves with complex multiplication by orders in the same imaginary quadratic field. We derive upper bounds for the primes of stable bad reduction of such curves in terms of the discriminants of the CM orders. To do so, we give an explicit description of principally polarized abelian surfaces with CM by a biquadratic field via small CM cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety of signature (3,2). We use it to prove an arithmetic intersection formula between such CM cycles with Humbert surfaces in terms of coefficients of incoherent Eisenstein series and representation numbers of ternary positive definite quadratic forms. Finally, employing the arithmetic properties of higher Green functions, we show that primes of stable bad reduction always exist.
item.dc:creator: Jan Hendrik Bruinier, Tonghai Yang, Peng Yu

item.title: A new proof of characteristic-free Kn\"orrer periodicity
item.description: arXiv:2609.37839v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $R = S/(f)$ be a complete local hypersurface ring and let $A = S[\![u,v]\!]/(f+uv)$. Pfister and Popescu showed that the stable categories of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules over $R$ and over $A$ are equivalent, with no assumption on the characteristic. We give a short proof. If $(\Phi,\Psi)$ is a matrix factorization of $h$ and $\partial$ is a derivation, then $(\partial\Psi,\partial\Phi)$ is a null-homotopy for multiplication by $\partial h$. Since $u$ and $v$ are partial derivatives of $f+uv$, they act as zero on the stable category of $A$, so the Koszul complex on $u$ and $v$ splits in the singularity category, and this gives density. For the double branched cover $S[\![z]\!]/(f+z^2)$ the same argument yields $2z$: it recovers Kn\"orrer's lemma up to free summands on the double branched cover when $2$ is a unit, and we show by an example that this lemma, and periodicity for the iterated double branched cover $S[\![z,w]\!]/(f+z^2+w^2)$, fail in characteristic two. We also compute the second syzygy over $A$ of a maximal Cohen-Macaulay $R$-module by an explicit resolution, and show that the change of basis used there cannot be given by a universal matrix formula.
item.dc:creator: Graham J. Leuschke

item.title: Some Remarks on Regular Sequences and Complete Intersections
item.description: arXiv:2610.15261v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an ideal in a polynomial ring in three variables, generated by three elements and having height equal to three, but for which no permutation of its generators is a regular sequence. We prove that in a polynomial ring over an infinite field, an ideal of height n generated by n polynomials, always admits a set of n generators, for which any permutation is a regular sequence.
item.dc:creator: Manolis C. Tsakiris

item.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.35037v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.
item.dc:creator: Jean Mousseau (LAMA)

item.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35492v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ be the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces of genus $g$ with $n$ cusps. The fixed-$n$ large-genus expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf has correction terms polynomial in $n$ of degree $2i$ at order $g^{-i}$, and ceases to be uniform when $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/g$ that holds uniformly in all $n\ge0$, with coefficients analytic in a density parameter that ranges over a compact interval, including the limits $n/g\to0$ and $n/g\to\infty$. Its leading term is explicit, contains no undetermined constant and has relative error $O(1/g)$; truncation at an order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$ this confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrt\pi$. We also determine, at every cusp density, the limits of the volume ratios $V_{g,n}/V_{g-1,n+2}$ and $V_{g,n+1}/(2gV_{g,n})$ and, in all degrees, the asymptotics of the ratios of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof deforms mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers into pure $\psi$ intersection numbers along a family whose recursion has nonnegative coefficients, fixes the overall constant through Painlev\'e I without assuming resurgence, and recovers individual volumes by a local limit theorem in the number of cusps. As an application, the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random surface with $n\gg\sqrt g$ cusps tends to zero in probability; this removes the restriction $n/g\to0$ from a theorem of Shen and Wu.
